'''Naranjan S. Dhalla''', {{Post-nominals|country=CAN|CM|OM|FRSC}} (born October 10, 1936) is a Canadian [[cardiovascular]] research scientist focusing on cardiovascular [[pathophysiology]] and [[cardiology|therapy]] of [[heart disease]]. His laboratory employs a variety of experimental models to investigate a wide range of cardiovascular diseases at the subcellular and molecular levels.

== History ==
Born in Ghanieke, [[Punjab (India)|Punjab]], [[India]], he received a [[Bachelor of Science]] in Physics and Chemistry from [[Panjab University, Chandigarh|Panjab University]] in 1956, an A.I.C. in Chemistry from the Institution of Chemists in [[Calcutta]], India in 1961, a Master of Science in Pharmacology from [[University of Pennsylvania]] in 1963, and a Ph.D. in Pharmacology from University of Pennsylvania in 1965. In 1968, he joined the [[University of Manitoba]] as an assistant professor in physiology. In 1972, he became an associate professor and a full professor in 1974. In 1991, he was appointed a distinguished professor of physiology.

From 1996 to 2006, he was the director of [[St. Boniface Hospital]] Research Centre's Institute of Cardiovascular Sciences. He last served as executive director of the International Academy of Cardiovascular Sciences.{{citation needed|date=November 2021}}

Dhalla also served the [[International Society for Heart Research]] as secretary general from 1972 to 1988, and as president elect, president, and past president from 1989 to 1998. He is credited for expanding the reach of the ISHR by establishing chapters in Russia, China, Japan, India, South America and in many other countries of the world.{{citation needed|date=November 2021}}

==Awards and honors==
In 1996, he was awarded Manitoba's [[Order of the Buffalo Hunt]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.gov.mb.ca/news/index.html?item=22697&posted=1996-10-19|title=Province of Manitoba &#124; Archived News Releases|website=News.gov.mb.ca|access-date=9 November 2021}}</ref> and the [[Order of Manitoba]] in 2002. In 1997, he was made a member of the [[Order of Canada]], Canada's highest civilian honour, for having "distinguished himself in the field of cardiovascular research".<ref>{{OCC|3747}}</ref> In 2000, he was made a fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]]. In 2007, he was granted heraldic arms from the [[Canadian Heraldic Authority]] with the motto "Satayam Shivam Sundaram" or "Truth Purity Beauty". In 2009, Dhalla was awarded an honorary doctorate from Panjab University, Chandigarh, India.{{citation needed|date=November 2021}} In 2019 he was inducted into the [[Canadian Medical Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cdnmedhall.ca/laureates/naranjandhalla |title=2019 Inductee, Naranjuan S. Dhalla, PhD |website=Canadian Medical Hall of Fame}}</ref>
